# Trunk Recorder Pro — building an interface (guide for an LLM)

You are building an interface for Trunk Recorder Pro, a program that records
public-safety radio (P25, SmartNet and DMR trunked systems, and conventional
FM / P25 / DMR channels) from software-defined radios. It runs a web server
(default http://localhost:8080). Everything its built-in interface does goes
through the API below, so you can build anything a user asks for: a
listening page, a wall display, a dashboard, a phone view, a program that
logs or forwards calls.

Read this whole file before writing code. The exact shape of every message
is in protocol.ts (GET /api/protocol.ts); when this guide and protocol.ts
disagree, protocol.ts is right. The human guide is README.md
(GET /api/docs).


## What to deliver

Unless the user asks otherwise, deliver an interface the recorder serves:

- A folder with an index.html, plus any other files it needs: plain HTML,
  CSS and JavaScript (ES modules). No build step, no frameworks, no CDN
  libraries unless the user asks for them.
- Import the client library from the recorder:
    import { TrunkClient, LivePlayer, escapeHtml } from "/api/client.js";
- Refer to your own files with relative paths ("./app.js", "style.css"). The
  folder is served at /ui/<name>/, or at / when it's the home interface.
- Refer to the recorder with absolute paths: /api/…, /calls/….
- Tell the user how to run it, in one of two ways:
    trunk-pro --ui /path/to/folder
      Shows it at http://localhost:8080/ for this run. The built-in
      interface stays at /builtin/.
    Setup → Recording → Interfaces → Add, then open /ui/<name>/.
      Or in the config: "server": {"interfaces": [{"name": "…", "path": "…"}],
      "home": "<name>"}.
  The recorder serves the files as they are on disk: edit, then reload.
- Make it work at phone width as well as on a desktop.

For a program rather than a page (logging, forwarding, alerts), write a
Node 22+ .mjs that imports a local copy of client.js. Node has WebSocket
built in. Programs need no access settings.

A page served from somewhere else (another machine, a dev server) needs its
origin in the recorder's config: "server": {"allowedOrigins":
["http://host:port"]}. It must import client.js by full URL, and pass
`new TrunkClient({ server: "host:port" })`. Prefer serving from the recorder.


## Template

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>…</title>
<style>/* … */</style>
</head>
<body>
<header><span id="conn">Connecting…</span> <button id="audio">Listen live</button></header>
<main id="main"></main>
<script type="module">
import { TrunkClient, LivePlayer, escapeHtml as esc, duration } from "/api/client.js";

const rec = new TrunkClient();
const player = new LivePlayer();
let listening = false;

document.getElementById("audio").onclick = async () => {
  listening = !listening;
  if (listening) { await player.resume(); rec.listen(); }   // audio needs a click first
  else { rec.listen(false); player.stop(); }
  draw();
};
rec.on("audio", (chunk) => player.play(chunk));
rec.on("change", draw);

function draw() {
  document.getElementById("conn").textContent = rec.connected ? `Recorder ${rec.phase.phase}` : "Reconnecting…";
  document.getElementById("audio").textContent = listening ? "Stop listening" : "Listen live";
  const now = rec.status?.nowS ?? 0;
  document.getElementById("main").innerHTML = rec.calls
    .map((c) => `<div>${esc(c.alphaTag || c.talkgroup)} · ${esc(c.systemName)} · ${duration(now - c.startS)}</div>`)
    .join("") || "Quiet";
}
draw();
</script>
</body>
</html>


## client.js (all of it)

new TrunkClient({ server?, secure?, historyLimit? })
  server defaults to the page's host; in Node, localhost:8080.
  It connects, reconnects by itself, and keeps this state (read only):
  connected   true while connected
  version     the recorder's version
  config      the whole config (Config)
  phase       { phase: "idle" | "starting" | "running" | "stopping", error: string|null, ended: boolean }
  status      EngineStatus while running, else null: { nowS, activeCalls, recording, callsConcluded, systems: SystemStatus[] }
  sources     SourceStatus[]: each radio (centerHz, rateHz, dropped, errors, errorPpm…)
  calls       CallView[]: the calls on the air now; [] when not running
  history     CallEntry[]: recorded calls, newest first (the last 300 at
              connect, plus each one recorded since; up to historyLimit)
  log         LogLine[]: the latest 500 log lines { timeS, kind, text, system? }
  error       the text of the latest error message, or null
  exited      true after the recorder said it was exiting; it keeps
              reconnecting (every 5 s), and this clears when it's back
 Events: rec.on(type, fn) returns a function that removes the handler.
  "change"      fn(rec): after every message. Redraw here.
  "<type>"      fn(message) for one message type, e.g. "concluded", "status", "state".
  "message"     fn(message): every message.
  "audio"       fn({ system, callId, talkgroup, samples: Float32Array /* 8000/s */ })
  "connection"  fn(true | false)
 Methods:
  rec.start() / rec.stop()           start / stop recording
  rec.listen()                       live audio of every call
  rec.listen({ talkgroup })          one talkgroup's
  rec.listen({ system, talkgroup })  one system's (its short name) talkgroup's
  rec.listen(false)                  none
                                     (kept across reconnects; one filter per connection)
  rec.setConfig((c) => { … })        change a copy of the config; the whole config is sent
  rec.callUrl(entry, "wav" | "json" | "m4a")   a recorded call's file URL
  rec.talkgroups(shortName)          Map talkgroup → { talkgroup, alphaTag, description, tag, group, mode }
  rec.unitName(shortName, unit)      a radio's name, or ""
  rec.send(message)                  any command (see Commands)
  rec.close()
new LivePlayer({ followCall = true, quietS = 1.5, gain = 2, onNowPlaying })
  await player.resume()   Call it in a click or key handler; browsers block audio otherwise.
  player.play(chunk)      Pass the "audio" chunks. followCall plays one call at
                          a time and skips calls that overlap it.
  player.nowPlaying       { callId, system, talkgroup } or null
  player.stop()
Helpers: escapeHtml(s), duration(seconds) → "1:05", mhz(hz) → "155.2000 MHz",
  parseTalkgroups(csv), decodeAudioFrame(arrayBuffer), CONVENTIONAL (65535),
  conventionalIndex(system).


## The data

CallView: a call on the air (rec.calls, from the "status" message)
  id, system (number), systemName (short name), talkgroup, alphaTag ("" if
  not in the talkgroup file), freqHz, slot, analog, tone, encrypted,
  emergency, startS (engine seconds), sources (unit numbers that talked,
  in order), state ("recording" | "monitoring"), reason (why it's only
  monitored: "ignored" | "unknown_tg" | "encrypted" | "no_source" |
  "no_recorder" | null), patched?, alsoOn?
  How long it's been going: rec.status.nowS - call.startS.

CallEntry: a recorded call (rec.history, the "concluded" message)
  { path, record }. path has no extension; the files are
  /calls/<path>.wav and .json (rec.callUrl(entry)).
  record is Trunk Recorder's call JSON (snake_case):
    talkgroup, talkgroup_tag, talkgroup_description, talkgroup_group,
    short_name (the system), start_time / stop_time (Unix seconds),
    start_time_ms, call_length (seconds of audio), freq (Hz),
    emergency (1/0), encrypted (1/0), audio_type ("analog" | "digital" |
    "digital tdma"), srcList [{ src (unit), tag (its name or ""), tag_ota,
    time (Unix s), pos (s into the audio), emergency }], signal / noise
    (dBFS) / snr (dB) (or null), tone_detected, patched_talkgroups?

SystemStatus: one trunked system or site (rec.status.systems)
  index (the `system` its calls carry), shortName, controlChannelHz,
  identity { nac, wacn, sysId, rfss, site }, good / bad (control messages
  decoded / failed: decode rate = good / (good + bad)), activeCalls,
  recording, callsConcluded, mismatch, adjacent, patches?, dmr?, siteGroup?

Systems and numbering
  config.systems[]: trunked systems ({ shortName, name?, type: "p25" |
    "smartnet" | "dmr", enabled, talkgroupsCsv, … }).
  config.conventional[k]: conventional systems. Their calls carry
    system = 65535 - k.
  Calls and audio carry `system` as a number. Match systems by short name
  (CallView.systemName, record.short_name, SystemStatus.shortName), not by
  position. Talkgroup numbers can repeat across systems: key talkgroups by
  (short name, talkgroup).

Times
  Engine seconds (nowS, startS, LogLine.timeS) count from when recording
  started. Call records use Unix seconds / ms. Frequencies are Hz
  everywhere.


## Messages and commands (only if you don't use client.js)

Connect to ws://<host>/api/ws. Text messages are JSON with a "type".
Binary messages are live audio:
  [u8 2][u16 system][u32 callId][u32 talkgroup][i16 samples…], little-endian, 8000/s.
From the recorder:
  hello        first; carries everything: version, config, phase, history (≤ 300), units, …
  plugins      second
  state        { phase, error, ended }: recording started / stopped
  status       ~2/s while running: { status, sources, load, calls }
  spectrum     ~7/s per radio: { source, centerHz, rateHz, bins: 512 dBFS levels }
  concluded    { entry }: a call was recorded
  log          { lines }
  unitAlias    { system (short name), unit, alias }
  config       { config }: someone changed the config
  error / notice  { message }: about your command
  quit         the recorder is exiting; keep reconnecting, slowly, in case it's restarted
  (more in protocol.ts; ignore types you don't use)
To the recorder:
  { type: "start" }, { type: "stop" }
  { type: "listen", on: true, system: null, talkgroup: null }   ("on" and both fields are always required)
  { type: "setConfig", config: <the whole config> }
  (more in protocol.ts: devices, survey, plugins, …)
Listening is per connection. Send listen again after every hello (each reconnect).


## Rules

1. Use field names exactly as given here or in protocol.ts. Don't invent
   fields or endpoints. There is no REST API for calls or talkgroups beyond
   what's listed here.
2. Escape everything that comes from the recorder before putting it in
   HTML: talkgroup names, unit names and aliases come from files and from
   the air. Use escapeHtml or textContent.
3. Never assume a field is set. alphaTag / talkgroup_tag can be "".
   status is null when not recording. Optional fields can be missing or
   null. Show the talkgroup number when there's no name.
4. Audio needs a user gesture. Call player.resume() inside a click handler
   before playing. A recorded call plays with <audio src=rec.callUrl(entry)>.
5. Everything is pushed. Don't poll, and don't fetch /calls/*.json for
   calls already in rec.history (the record is there).
6. Only change the config, or start / stop recording, when the user asks for
   that feature. Do it with a visible control, through rec.setConfig /
   rec.start / rec.stop. Never build a config from scratch: fields left out
   reset to defaults.
7. History reaches back 300 calls at connect, and grows as calls are
   recorded. Older recordings are on disk, but there's no API to list them.
   Say so if the user asks for more.
8. One live-audio filter per connection: one talkgroup, or everything. For
   several talkgroups, listen to everything and drop the chunks you don't
   want before player.play.
9. Keep the page alive through disconnects and restarts. Show the
   connection state (rec.connected, rec.exited); client.js reconnects by
   itself.
10. The API has no login. Don't put the recorder on the internet. If the user
    wants remote access, tell them to use a VPN, an SSH tunnel, or a reverse
    proxy with authentication.


## Before you finish

- It runs from the recorder: `trunk-pro --ui <folder>` → http://localhost:8080/.
- With the recorder idle, it shows the history and a clear idle state, not
  an error.
- While recording, it updates without reloading.
- It survives the recorder restarting: it reconnects and redraws.
- Live audio starts from a click, and stops.
- It's usable on a phone-width screen.
- Every piece of recorder text is escaped.

Working examples to copy from (GET /api/examples/<file>):
  scanner.html    everything, without client.js (the raw protocol)
  wall.html       a wall display with client.js
  talkgroup.html  follow one talkgroup: live, recordings, play new ones as they come
  call-log.mjs    Node: append calls to a CSV file and POST them to a webhook
